name: Count Pairs
description: You are given a prime number $$$p$$$, $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$, and an integer $$$k$$$. Find the number of pairs of indexes $$$(i, j)$$$ ($$$1 \le i \lt j \le n$$$) for which $$$(a_i + a_j)(a_i^2 + a_j^2) \equiv k \bmod p$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains integers $$$n, p, k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$2 \le p \le 10^9$$$, $$$0 \le k \le p-1$$$). $$$p$$$ is guaranteed to be prime. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le p-1$$$). It is guaranteed that all elements are different.
output_specification: Output a single integer — answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1188B — Count Pairs [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
